artiest/felix-da-housecat.text:
Felix da Housecat is the stage name of Felix Stallings Jr., an American DJ and producer from the Chicago area, born in 1971. He belongs to the second generation of Chicago house. As a fifteen-year-old schoolboy in Park Forest he came into contact with the acid house pioneer DJ Pierre, who helped him get started. His first single, Phantasy Girl, appeared in 1987. He then studied media and communications and became interested in hip hop and R&B.

In the 1990s he released work under various names, including Aphrohead and Thee Maddkatt Courtship. He founded the label Radikal Fear. His breakthrough to a wide audience came in 2001 with Kittenz and Thee Glitz, an album he made with Miss Kittin and Tommie Sunshine, among others. At the end of that year it won the prize for best album at the Muzik Awards. After that he made remixes for Madonna, Britney Spears and Kylie Minogue. Later albums were Devin Dazzle and the Neon Fever in 2004, Virgo Blaktro and the Movie Disco in 2007 and He Was King in 2009.

His music combines house with the cool, synthetic sound of electroclash. Silver Screen (Shower Scene) was used in video games and in the film Kiss Kiss Bang Bang. Felix da Housecat shows how Chicago house developed, in the years around 2000, into a glamorous, nightlife-oriented form of pop.
artiest/felix-da-housecat.listen: Listen to Silver Screen (Shower Scene) and notice the tight, electronic rhythm and the cool, almost robotic vocals. Which sounds keep returning, and how does the track build?

artiest/felix-mendelssohn.text:
Felix Mendelssohn Bartholdy was a German composer, conductor and pianist of the early nineteenth century. He was born in Hamburg in 1809 and grew up in Berlin, where he stood out as a child prodigy. In 1836 he met the singer Cécile Jeanrenaud in Frankfurt, and he married her in 1837. He settled in Leipzig, where the first of their five children was born. His sister Fanny was also a composer.

Among his best-known works are the music for A Midsummer Night's Dream, the Italian Symphony, the Violin Concerto in E minor, Op. 64, and the Songs Without Words for piano. The recordings in the archive begin in 1953 and show how often the Violin Concerto and A Midsummer Night's Dream in particular have been recorded, often coupled with works by Beethoven, Mozart and Tchaikovsky.

Mendelssohn's music is clear, graceful and full of melody, with refined orchestration, and it joins classicism to Romanticism. He was also a conductor who brought older music, including that of Bach, to the public's attention. His work is therefore a source of the way we still hear and play classical concert music today. He died in Leipzig in 1847.
artiest/felix-mendelssohn.listen: Listen to the Violin Concerto in E minor and notice how the soloist enters after only a few bars with a fiery, singing melody, without a long orchestral introduction.

artiest/femi-koleoso.text: The drummer Femi Koleoso is the leader of Ezra Collective, which he founded in north London with his brother, the bassist TJ Koleoso. The band members met through Tomorrow's Warriors. Ezra Collective blends jazz with Afrobeat, hip hop, grime and Caribbean music, and plays for a dancing audience. In 2023 the band won the Mercury Prize with Where I'm Meant to Be, the first jazz group to do so. Koleoso also plays drums with Gorillaz and is a well-known advocate of music education for young people.
artiest/femi-koleoso.listen: Follow the drums: Afrobeat and jazz in a single groove.

artiest/feminist-improvising-group.text:
The Feminist Improvising Group, FIG for short, was an international ensemble of five to eight players for free improvisation and experimental music. The Scottish singer Maggie Nicols and the English bassoonist and composer Lindsay Cooper founded it in London in 1977. They discussed the idea at a meeting of the musicians' union. According to Cooper there was a lot of improvisation, but no women took part, so they decided to do it themselves. The debut took place in October 1977 at the Music for Socialism festival at the Almost Free Theatre. The group then toured Europe several times, in the late 1970s and early 1980s.

FIG was the first women's improvisation group to perform in public. The members had different backgrounds and different levels of experience, and the concerts combined music and theatre about everyday women's issues. Lesbian sexuality was also part of the performances. Many male improvisers reacted dismissively and found the technique inadequate. Some feminists, on the other hand, found it too virtuosic and abstract. The audience mostly responded positively. In 1983 FIG continued as the European Women's Improvising Group, after pressure had arisen to tone down the name. The album Another Evening at Logos, from 2015, contains recordings from 1974, 1979 and 1981.

The group was influential for the second generation of improvisers and led to more women's groups and events. It introduced new audiences to improvisation and to feminism.
artiest/feminist-improvising-group.listen: Listen to an excerpt of Another Evening at Logos and notice how voices and instruments play in and out of one another, without a fixed melody, and how the sound sometimes resembles theatre.

artiest/ferry-corsten.text:
Ferry Corsten was born in Rotterdam in 1973. As a child he listened to radio programmes featuring disco, soul and electronic music, and he bought the records he liked. At fifteen he DJed for the first time, at school parties. By washing cars and selling homemade mixtapes he saved up for his first synthesizer. In the Rotterdam of the 1990s he first made gabber and hardcore, and later house and trance. Meanwhile he trained as an electrical engineer.

Corsten worked under many different names. As Moonman he reached the UK chart in 1996 with Don't Be Afraid. In 1997 he started the label Tsunami with Robert Smit. The big breakthrough came in 1999 as System F, with Out of the Blue, a worldwide trance hit. That same year, with Tiësto as Gouryella he made the hits Gouryella and Walhalla, and with Vincent de Moor as Veracocha the track Carte Blanche. He became a sought-after remixer, for U2, Moby and William Orbit, among others. His remix of Adagio for Strings won an award, and his mix CD in Ministry of Sound's Trance Nation series was a great success.

Corsten makes melodic electronic dance music in which synthesizer melodies play the leading role. Like Tiësto and Armin van Buuren, he was one of the Dutch DJs who reached the top of the world scene. In 2004 and 2005 he was ranked fifth on DJ Mag's list of best DJs. Later he broadened his style to progressive house. In 2022 he was made an Officer of the Order of Orange-Nassau.
artiest/ferry-corsten.listen: Listen to Out of the Blue by System F and notice how it builds. Hear how the track grows layer by layer and how the synthesizer melody becomes the recognisable centrepiece.

artiest/finneas-o-connell.text:
Finneas O'Connell was born in Los Angeles on 30 July 1997. His parents are both actors and musicians. At twelve he took a songwriting course with his mother, and from then on he wrote and produced songs himself. As a teenager he also worked as an actor, appearing in the television series Glee, among other things.

His best-known work was made with his younger sister Billie Eilish. He wrote and produced all of her music with her, including her debut album When We All Fall Asleep, Where Do We Go? (2019). It earned him Grammys including album of the year, and he became the youngest ever winner of the producer of the year award. With Eilish he also wrote No Time to Die for the Bond film of the same name, and What Was I Made For? Both songs won an Oscar. He also worked with artists such as Selena Gomez, Justin Bieber, Rosalía and even Ringo Starr, and composed film music. As a solo artist he released the albums Optimist (2021) and For Cryin' Out Loud! (2024).

O'Connell says that his experience as an actor helps him when writing for others: he tries to write from their voice, their words and their range. When he writes with his sister, he mainly wants to help tell the story she wants to tell. That close collaboration between brother and sister, without a big studio or a team of writers, made them one of the most successful duos in pop this century.
artiest/finneas-o-connell.listen: Listen to bad guy by Billie Eilish (2019), produced by Finneas. Notice how little happens in the song: a deep synthesizer bass, dry clicks and Eilish's soft, almost whispered voice. Listen too for the unexpected turning point at the end.

artiest/fischerspooner.text:
Fischerspooner was an electroclash duo and performance group, formed in New York in 1998 by Warren Fischer and Casey Spooner. The name is a contraction of their surnames. Fischer was a classically trained musician, Spooner a video artist and experimental theatre maker. They began with an improvised performance of their song Indian Cab Driver in a Starbucks on Astor Place. From this grew a company of more than twenty performing dancers and guest singers. The project began as a performance artwork about entertainment.

The debut album #1 was released around 2001 on several labels, including International DJ Gigolo, Ministry of Sound and Capitol Records. It contains Sweetness, Emerge and a cover of The 15th by Wire. In 2005 came Odyssey, which sounded more like electropop than electroclash, with Just Let Go and Never Win. Then came Entertainment in 2009, produced by Jeff Saltzman, and Sir in 2018, on which Michael Stipe of R.E.M. collaborated.

The music is cool and synthetic, with a deliberately theatrical look. Fischerspooner belonged to the New York scene in which synth-pop, club music and art came together, and showed that a show could be just as important as the song itself. The group belongs to the wave that, around 2001, gave electronic dance music a pop image again.
artiest/fischerspooner.listen: Listen to Emerge and notice the electronic sounds and the aloof, almost theatrical vocals. Can you hear how the track relies more on atmosphere and repetition than on a classic song structure?

artiest/fisk-university-jubilee-quartet.text:
The Fisk Jubilee Singers are an African American a cappella ensemble of students from Fisk University in Nashville, Tennessee. The university was founded after the Civil War to educate freed slaves and other young Black Americans. In 1871 the money threatened to run out. Treasurer and music director George Leonard White, a white missionary from the North, put together a choir of nine students to raise money on tour. On 6 October 1871 that tour began in Cincinnati, with two quartets and a pianist.

The first repertoire consisted mainly of traditional spirituals, supplemented by a few songs by Stephen Foster. The singers travelled through the United States and also went to Europe, where other groups performed later in the nineteenth century. After a concert in Cincinnati they donated their small profit to the victims of the great Chicago fire. The quartet made a recording of Swing Low, Sweet Chariot in 1909. In 2002 the Library of Congress added that recording to the National Recording Registry. In 2008 the Jubilee Singers received the National Medal of Arts.

The singing is in several parts and unaccompanied, with a warm, calm blend of voices. The group made the spiritual, the song of the slaves, known to a white audience and showed that this music was an art form in its own right. In doing so it laid a foundation for much later American popular music, from gospel to soul. In School of Rock the 1909 recording is one of the earliest sound examples.
artiest/fisk-university-jubilee-quartet.listen: Listen to the 1909 recording of Swing Low, Sweet Chariot. Notice the four voices without any instrument, how the bass carries the bottom and how the singing stays calm and even.

artiest/fivio-foreign.text:
Fivio Foreign is the stage name of Maxie Lee Ryles III, an American rapper from Brooklyn, born on 29 March 1990. He grew up in East Flatbush. In 2011 he began rapping under the name Lite Fivio; two years later he changed it to Fivio Foreign and founded the collective 800 Foreign Side with friends.

His breakthrough came in 2019 with the single Big Drip, which was certified platinum by the RIAA and led to a remix with Lil Baby and Quavo. The track appears on the EPs Pain and Love from 2019 and 800 B.C. from 2020. At the end of 2019 he signed to Mase's label, RichFish Records. In 2020 he entered the Billboard Hot 100 for the first time with guest appearances on Demons by Drake and Zoo York by Lil Tjay, and he was included in the XXL Freshman Class. He also worked with Kanye West, on Off the Grid from 2021 among others. His debut album B.I.B.L.E. appeared in 2022, followed by Pain & Love 2 in 2024 and Still Standing in 2026.

Fivio Foreign belongs to the New York drill scene, a style with hard, dark beats and a raw, shouted delivery. He showed that Brooklyn drill, which was on the rise in 2019 and 2020, could reach a large audience outside the city too. With his short, catchy lines he became a face of that generation.
artiest/fivio-foreign.listen: Listen to Big Drip and notice the rhythm of the voice: Fivio raps in short, punchy phrases over a dark, heavy beat. Which line sticks in your head after one listen?

artiest/flatt-en-scruggs.text:
Flatt & Scruggs was the duo of singer and guitarist Lester Flatt and banjo player Earl Scruggs. Both grew up in the rural American South, Flatt in Tennessee and Scruggs in North Carolina, and both worked in the textile industry as boys. From 1945 they played together in Bill Monroe's Blue Grass Boys, the band from which bluegrass takes its name. In early 1948 they left and formed their own group, the Foggy Mountain Boys, named after the misty mountains of the Appalachians.

In 1949 they recorded Foggy Mountain Breakdown, an instrumental by Scruggs with lightning-fast playing on the five-string banjo. Scruggs was one of the first to pick the banjo with three fingers, which gave the instrument a melodic lead role. Together with Flatt's rhythm guitar and vocals, the fiddle, mandolin, bass and later Josh Graves's dobro, that gave the group a distinctive, driving sound. In 1955 they became members of the Grand Ole Opry. In 1962 they scored their only number one on the country charts with The Ballad of Jed Clampett, the theme tune of the TV series The Beverly Hillbillies.

Through the folk revival they also reached a young, urban audience. Foggy Mountain Breakdown was heard in the 1967 film Bonnie and Clyde and won a Grammy. Scruggs wanted to innovate, Flatt held on to the old style, and in 1969 they split up. The duo has been in the Country Music Hall of Fame since 1985.
artiest/flatt-en-scruggs.listen: Watch Foggy Mountain Breakdown and follow Earl Scruggs's banjo. Notice how quickly the notes follow one another, and how the banjo, guitar and fiddle take over the melody in turn.

artiest/flavor-flav.text:
Flavor Flav's real name is William Drayton, and he was born in 1959 in Roosevelt, New York. He grew up in nearby Freeport, where his father had a restaurant. At the age of five he taught himself to play the piano, and as a child he also played drums and guitar and sang in the church choir. According to Chuck D he plays fifteen instruments. At Adelphi University he met Carlton Ridenhour, the later Chuck D. They first worked together on Chuck's hip hop programme on the university radio station and then began rapping together. His stage name was originally his graffiti name.

In 1985 they founded Public Enemy together. Producer Rick Rubin of Def Jam at first wanted to sign only Chuck D, but he insisted that Flav came along. After the debut Yo! Bum Rush the Show (1987) came It Takes a Nation of Millions to Hold Us Back (1988) and the single Fight the Power (1989). With 911 Is a Joke Flav had his first hit as a solo rapper in 1990.

In Public Enemy Flavor Flav was the hype man: he whipped up the crowd, shouted in between and formed the comic counterpart to the serious, political Chuck D. On stage he stood out with big hats, glasses and a large clock around his neck, and with his catchphrase Yeah, boyeee! He made the role of the hype man known to a large audience. Later he became best known for reality series on TV. With Public Enemy he was inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame.
artiest/flavor-flav.listen: Listen to 911 Is a Joke by Public Enemy, in which Flavor Flav himself takes the lead. Notice his playful, mocking way of rapping, and compare it with the heavy, serious voice of Chuck D in Fight the Power.

artiest/flea.text:
Flea's real name is Michael Balzary, and he was born in Melbourne, Australia, in 1962. When he was four the family moved to New York, and after his parents' divorce he went with his mother and stepfather, a jazz musician, to Los Angeles. There he played the trumpet and idolised Miles Davis, Louis Armstrong and Dizzy Gillespie. Rock did not interest him. His childhood at home was violent. At Fairfax High School Anthony Kiedis became his best friend, and the guitarist Hillel Slovak taught him to play bass guitar.

With Kiedis, Slovak and the drummer Jack Irons he founded the Red Hot Chili Peppers. Their debut was released in 1984, and for the second album, Freaky Styley (1985), they chose the funk musician George Clinton as producer. The big successes came later, with albums such as Blood Sugar Sex Magik, Californication and Stadium Arcadium. Flea also played with Johnny Cash, Tom Waits, Nirvana and Jane's Addiction, among others, and was in Atoms for Peace. He also appeared in films such as Back to the Future Part II and The Big Lebowski.

Flea's bass playing mixes funk, punk, psychedelia and hard rock. Striking is his slap bass: he hits the strings with his thumb and pulls them with his fingers, so that the bass sounds like a percussion instrument. In this way the bass is often at the front of the Chili Peppers' music. Readers of Rolling Stone chose him in 2009 as the second-best bassist of all time. In 2012 he was inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame with the band. He also founded a music school for children from poor families.
artiest/flea.listen: Listen to Give It Away by the Red Hot Chili Peppers and notice Flea's bass. Hear how he hits the strings hard, so that the bass sounds almost like a drum, while Anthony Kiedis raps over it more than he sings.

artiest/fleet-foxes.text:
Fleet Foxes is an American indie folk and folk rock band from Seattle, formed in 2006. Robin Pecknold and Skyler Skjelset, two friends from the same high school in Kirkland, began making music together out of admiration for Bob Dylan, Neil Young and Brian Wilson. At first the band was called The Pineapples. The name Fleet Foxes came after it turned out that another local group had the same name. Pecknold became the main songwriter and singer, Skjelset played lead guitar. Later Casey Wescott, Christian Wargo and Morgan Henderson, among others, joined.

Producer Phil Ek helped them with a first demo in 2006. After the EP Sun Giant, the debut album Fleet Foxes was released on Sub Pop in 2008, with White Winter Hymnal. The album received rave reviews and was well received in Europe. In 2011 came Helplessness Blues, their greatest commercial success, which reached number 4 on the Billboard 200 in the United States. After a three-year break came Crack-Up in 2017 and Shore in 2020.

The band's sound centres on rich harmony singing and refined instrumentation, with acoustic guitars, mandolin, keyboards and plenty of reverb. The style is inspired by the pop music of the late 1960s. In the 2000s Fleet Foxes showed that folk could once again reach a large indie audience, and it contributed to the revival of harmonic folk pop.
artiest/fleet-foxes.listen: Listen to White Winter Hymnal and count how many voices are singing at once. Notice how the singing passes the melody around and how few instruments are needed.

artiest/fleetwood-mac.text:
Fleetwood Mac was formed in London in July 1967 by the guitarist Peter Green, shortly after he had left John Mayall & the Bluesbreakers. The drummer Mick Fleetwood and the guitarist Jeremy Spencer played with him from the start, and the bassist John McVie joined within a few weeks. In ten years the band went from British blues to American soft rock.

In the early years Fleetwood Mac was mainly a blues band. The instrumental Albatross, released at the end of 1968, reached number 1 in England in January 1969. In 1970 Green left, and that same year the singer and keyboard player Christine McVie became a member. On New Year's Eve 1974 the guitarist Lindsey Buckingham and the singer Stevie Nicks joined. With them the sound became more melodic and lighter. The album Fleetwood Mac (1975) reached number 1 in America. Rumours (1977) was recorded while the relationships within the band were falling apart. The first single, Go Your Own Way, was written by Buckingham about his break-up with Nicks. It became the band's first American top-ten hit. Rumours won a Grammy for album of the year. By 2003 it had sold forty million copies worldwide.

After that, with the double album Tusk (1979), the band chose a stranger, rawer sound. Tango in the Night (1987) was another great success. In 1998 Fleetwood Mac was inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame. Christine McVie died in 2022. Rumours is a textbook example of soft rock: smooth production, strong vocal melodies and lyrics about the band members' own lives.
artiest/fleetwood-mac.listen: For Go Your Own Way, Buckingham wanted the drum feel of Street Fighting Man by The Rolling Stones. Mick Fleetwood made his own version of it, across the toms and with the bass drum in an unexpected place in the middle of the bar. Listen to how that rhythm gives the song a restless momentum.

artiest/fletcher-henderson.text: Fletcher Henderson came from Georgia, studied chemistry and ended up in music in New York. From 1924 he led an orchestra at the Roseland Ballroom that laid the foundation for the big band. With the arranger Don Redman he divided the band into sections that answered one another. In 1924 and 1925 Louis Armstrong played in the band, which taught the musicians to swing. Coleman Hawkins also played there for years. Henderson was a poor businessman and lost his orchestra in the mid-1930s. He sold his arrangements to Benny Goodman, who had great success with them, and later also worked as Goodman's arranger. He died in 1952.
artiest/fletcher-henderson.listen: Hear how the saxophones play a melody and the brass answer with short stabs.

artiest/flip-phillips.text:
Joseph Edward Filippelli, known as Flip Phillips, was an American jazz saxophonist on tenor and a clarinettist. He was born in Brooklyn in 1915. In the 1930s he played clarinet in a restaurant in Brooklyn. After that he worked in the bands of Frankie Newton, Red Norvo, Benny Goodman and Wingy Manone. In the mid-1940s he was a regular soloist in Woody Herman's band, the First Herd.

His best-known period came after that, from 1946 to 1957, in the Jazz at the Philharmonic concerts of Norman Granz. In those years he also played on recordings by Charlie Parker. He recorded a great deal for Clef Records, including a 1949 album with his own small group, in which Kai Winding, Sonny Criss, Ray Brown and Shelly Manne, among others, played. In 1952 he accompanied Billie Holiday on Billie Holiday Sings. He withdrew to Florida, but after fifteen years returned to New York and continued to record and perform into his eighties, with A Sound Investment in 1987, Swing Is The Thing! in 2000 and Mayhem In Manhattan in 2003, among others. He died in Fort Lauderdale in 2001.

Phillips played mainstream jazz, swing and jump blues. In the Dutch description he is called an impulsive tenor saxophonist of the swing era. His playing is energetic, with a big, warm tone, and made him a favourite of the audiences in Granz's concert halls. He belongs to the generation that passed swing on to the jazz of the postwar years.
artiest/flip-phillips.listen: Listen to a recording of Flip Phillips with Jazz at the Philharmonic, or to Mood Indigo, and notice the full, warm tone of the tenor saxophone and the energetic, swinging phrasing.

artiest/floating-points.text:
Floating Points is the stage name of Samuel Thomas Shepherd, a British producer, DJ and musician, born in 1986 and raised in Manchester. He studied piano at Chetham's School of Music and then completed a doctorate at University College London in neuroscience and epigenetics, with research into pain responses. In the late 2000s he DJed at the London club Plastic People. In 2008 he started the label Eglo Records with Alexander Nut, and in 2015 he founded Pluto Records himself.

His first release was the Vacuum EP in 2008. In 2010 he played live with a sixteen-piece group, the Floating Points Ensemble, which received an award for best BBC Radio 1 Maida Vale Session. His first album, Elaenia, was released on 6 November 2015 and received mostly glowing reviews. Crush followed in 2019, Promises in 2020 and Cascade in 2024. In 2017 he toured with The xx and made Reflections: Mojave Desert. He remixed Thundercat, Caribou and Basement Jaxx, among others.

His music combines electronic dance music with jazz, classical and ambient. He names Claude Debussy, Olivier Messiaen and Bill Evans as influences. On Promises he collaborated with the saxophonist Pharoah Sanders and the London Symphony Orchestra. In this way he belongs to the producers who enriched electronic music with acoustic instruments and a broad musical education.
artiest/floating-points.listen: Listen to a track from Elaenia and notice how synthesizers, piano and electronic rhythms slowly flow into one another and form a warm, floating sound.

artiest/flora-purim.text: The singer Flora Purim grew up in Rio de Janeiro and sang in the bossa nova scene there. In 1967 she left for the United States with her husband, the percussionist Airto Moreira. She sang in the first line-up of Chick Corea's Return to Forever, on What Game Shall We Play Today and Light as a Feather, among others. She used her voice as an instrument, with a wide range and wordless sounds. In 1974 she was convicted of drug possession and spent some time in prison; afterwards she made several albums. In the 1970s she was voted best singer several times in DownBeat magazine.
artiest/flora-purim.listen: Listen to the voice moving between words and sounds.

artiest/florian-schneider.text:
Florian Schneider was born in 1947 in Öhningen, on Lake Constance in southern Germany. His father was an architect. When Florian was three, the family moved to Düsseldorf. In 1968, while studying, he met Ralf Hütter. Together they played improvised music in the group Organisation, with Schneider on flute and Hütter on Hammond organ. In 1970 they founded Kraftwerk together in Düsseldorf.

At first the flute was his main instrument. Schneider shaped the sound with electronic effects such as tape echo, ring modulator, fuzz and wah-wah, so that his flute could even sound like a bass instrument. He also played violin and electric guitar, and used synthesizers. After the album Autobahn (1974) the acoustic instruments gradually disappeared from his playing. Later he said that he found the flute too limiting: first he bought a microphone, then loudspeakers, an echo unit and a synthesizer, until he finally got rid of the flute.

Schneider was above all a sound designer. Hütter called him a perfectionist who was only satisfied when the sound was exactly right. He worked a great deal with the vocoder and with speech synthesis, and developed the Robovox, one of Kraftwerk's characteristic sounds. In this way he contributed to the image of Kraftwerk as man-machine. David Bowie named an instrumental on his album Heroes after him: V-2 Schneider. Schneider last played with Kraftwerk in 2006 and left the group in 2008. He died in 2020.
artiest/florian-schneider.listen: Listen to a Kraftwerk track in which a robotic voice sings or speaks, such as Die Roboter. Notice how the human voice has been changed electronically, the field in which Schneider specialised.

artiest/flume.text:
Flume is the stage name of Harley Edward Streten, an Australian musician, DJ and producer, born in 1991 in Sydney. He grew up on the Northern Beaches. His father is a film-maker and producer, his mother a horticulturalist. At eleven he began making music with a simple DJ program that came in a box of cornflakes. It showed him how music is built up in layers. In 2010 he made house under the name HEDS. He got his first radio play with Possum, which he put on Triple J Unearthed. In 2011 he signed to the label Future Classic through a competition and released the EP Sleepless. He chose the name Flume after a song by Bon Iver.

His first album, Flume, was released in 2012 and topped the Australian album chart. Skin followed in 2016, also number one in Australia, and in 2017 won a Grammy for best dance/electronic album. The single Never Be Like You was nominated for best dance recording. After that came Skin Companion EP 1 and 2, the mixtape Hi This Is Flume in 2019, Palaces in 2022 and the mixtapes Things Don't Always Go the Way You Plan and Arrived Anxious, Left Bored in 2023. He remixed Lorde, Sam Smith, Arcade Fire and Disclosure, among others.

Flume is regarded as a pioneer of future bass, a style with warped synthesizers, heavy bass and chopped vocal samples. He helped make that genre popular. His music shows how a bedroom producer from Australia gained worldwide influence on electronic pop music.
artiest/flume.listen: Listen to Never Be Like You from Skin and notice how the sampled vocals are chopped up and worked into the beat, with heavy bass and glittering synthesizers.

artiest/flying-lotus.text: Steven Ellison, known as Flying Lotus, is a producer from Los Angeles. Alice Coltrane was his great-aunt, and he names her music and that of John Coltrane as a major influence, alongside J Dilla. In 2008 he founded the label Brainfeeder. His album Cosmogramma (2010) mixes electronic beats, jazz, harp and strings. On You're Dead! (2014) Herbie Hancock, Thundercat and Kamasi Washington played; Kendrick Lamar raps on Never Catch Me. Flying Lotus also made music for films and anime, and made the film Kuso.
artiest/flying-lotus.listen: Hear how electronic beats and real jazz instruments flow into one another.

artiest/focus.text:
Focus is a Dutch progressive rock band from Amsterdam. The keyboard player, singer and flautist Thijs van Leer founded the group in 1969, together with the drummer Hans Cleuver, the bassist Martijn Dresden and the guitarist Jan Akkerman. They first played in the orchestra of the Dutch production of the musical Hair. Focus then became a band in its own right, which released the debut album Focus Plays Focus in 1970. Later in 1970 the drummer Pierre van der Linden joined.

The debut went almost unnoticed, but the second album, Moving Waves, from 1971, brought the international breakthrough. It reached number 2 in the United Kingdom and number 8 in the United States. The lead single Hocus Pocus made the group known worldwide. Focus 3 followed in 1972, Hamburger Concerto in 1974 and Mother Focus in 1975. Van Leer brought the band back together in 2002, and in 2024 Focus 12 appeared.

Focus combines progressive rock with jazz, classical music and long solos. Akkerman plays guitar, Van Leer flute and organ, and there are pieces with high, yodel-like singing. In this way the band gave the rock of those years a sound of its own. Focus is regarded as one of the most successful and influential rock bands from the Netherlands.
artiest/focus.listen: Listen to Hocus Pocus and notice how the guitar riff, the flute and the unusual vocal sounds alternate. Which part surprises you most in such a short track?

artiest/foday-musa-suso.text:
Foday Musa Suso was a Gambian musician and composer, born on 18 February 1950 and died on 25 May 2025. He came from the Mandinka and was a griot. Griots are the oral historians and musicians of the Mandingo in West Africa. They are a living library for their community and pass on history, entertainment and wisdom in song and playing. Suso was descended from Jali Madi Wuleng Suso, the griot who is said to have invented the kora more than four centuries ago. He grew up in a traditional village in Gambia, in a house full of kora music.

In 1977 he left for Chicago, and was thus one of the first jalis to settle in North America. There, with the percussionists Hamid Drake and Adam Rudolph, he formed the Mandingo Griot Society, which played fusion music. His first albums were Kora Music From The Gambia from 1978 and Hand Power from 1984. He worked with Bill Laswell and Philip Glass. His electrified kora can be heard on Herbie Hancock's Sound-System from 1984, and the following year Suso and Hancock made the duo album Village Life, with synthesizer, kora, talking drum and vocals.

Suso brought the kora, a West African stringed instrument with a clear, harp-like sound, to jazz, electronica and minimalist music. In this way he showed that a centuries-old griot tradition could take part in modern popular music. Sunjata, the piece from the course, refers to the epic of the founder of the Mali Empire, which griots have told for centuries.
artiest/foday-musa-suso.listen: Listen to Sunjata and follow the kora: notice how the strings play a continuous pattern, with the melody and the voice coming on top of it.

artiest/fonce-mizell.text:
Alphonso Fonce Mizell was an American producer and songwriter, born in 1943 and died in 2011. He worked with his brother Larry Mizell, born in 1944, as the Mizell Brothers. Fonce studied music at Howard University, Larry engineering. At that university they formed the jazz vocal quartet the Vanlords. At the beginning of the 1970s they moved to California and started their own company, Sky High Productions.

For Blue Note Records they produced albums that set the tone for the jazz fusion of that time, including with Johnny Hammond Smith, Roger Glenn, The Blackbyrds and Donald Byrd. They often used the same musicians, such as the drummer Harvey Mason, the percussionist Mayuto Correa, the guitarists Wah Wah Watson and David T. Walker, the bassist Chuck Rainey and the pianist Jerry Peters. Later came hits such as Boogie Oogie Oogie by A Taste of Honey in 1978, Love Ballad by L.T.D. in 1976, which reached number one on the R&B chart, and Gigolo by Mary Wells in 1982. On Donald Byrd's albums they also worked in Motown hits, such as Just My Imagination and Dancing in the Street.

Before Fonce went his own way, he was with The Corporation, Motown's writing and production team that made the early hits of The Jackson 5, from 1969 to 1971, such as I Want You Back and ABC. In this way he linked the smooth soul of Motown to the jazz and disco of the 1970s. In the 1980s the brothers withdrew from the record industry; in the 2000s they returned.
artiest/fonce-mizell.listen: Listen to a Donald Byrd track from the 1970s, such as Dancing in the Street, and notice how jazz trumpet, soft vocals, bass and drums form a smooth, danceable groove.

artiest/fong-naam.text:
Fong Naam is a Thai orchestra that plays and renews classical Thai music. The group was founded by Boonyong Ketkong and Jirapan Ansvananda, together with the American musician Bruce Gaston. Gaston, born in Los Angeles, studied at the University of Southern California and went to work in Thailand instead of serving in the army. He lived there until his death in 2021 and helped develop a contemporary form of classical Thai music.

Traditional Thai orchestras consist of melodic percussion instruments, such as xylophones and gong circles, supplemented by strings, flutes and drums. Their music has no chords as in the West: several instruments play variations on the same melody, which run through one another in layers. The orchestra's pieces in the course, Sathukarn, Tra Yapakkok and Tra Jomsri from 1991, come from this classical tradition.

For anyone who listens to pop, Fong Naam is a source for hearing that rhythm, melody and ensemble playing can also be organised differently. The orchestra shows how an old court music came back to life in the twentieth century, partly thanks to the contribution of a foreign musician. Little is recorded in our sources about the precise history and line-up.
artiest/fong-naam.listen: Listen to Sathukarn and notice how the melodic percussionists play one melody while other instruments ornament it in their own way. Is there a steady pulse that you can tap along to?

artiest/fontella-bass.text:
Fontella Bass was an American R&B and soul singer and songwriter, born in 1940 in St. Louis, Missouri. She was the daughter of the gospel singer Martha Bass, who sang with the Clara Ward Singers, and the older sister of the singer David Peaston. At five she accompanied her grandmother's singing at funerals on the piano, at six she sang in the church choir, and at nine she went on tour with her mother through the South and Southwest. At seventeen she began performing professionally at the Showboat Club. Through the singer Little Milton and the bandleader Oliver Sain she joined the band, first as a pianist, then as a singer.

She recorded for Bobbin Records and was produced by Ike Turner. Her 1964 single Poor Little Fool had Tina Turner as a backing singer, but had little success. Her big hit came in 1965 with Rescue Me, which reached number one on the R&B chart. She married the jazz trumpeter Lester Bowie and worked with the Art Ensemble of Chicago, which led to the album Art Ensemble of Chicago With Fontella Bass in 1971. After that came Free in 1972, No Ways Tired in 1995 and Rescue Me in 2005, among others. She also worked with The Cinematic Orchestra.

Bass received two Grammy nominations and a place on the St. Louis Walk of Fame. Her voice combines the power of gospel with the tight backing of 1960s soul. In this way she linked church, soul and avant-garde jazz. She died in 2012.
artiest/fontella-bass.listen: Listen to Rescue Me and notice her powerful, direct voice and the tight bass line and horns that make the song swing.

artiest/foo-fighters.text:
The Foo Fighters are an American rock band, formed in Seattle in 1994. It began as a solo project by Dave Grohl, the former drummer of Nirvana, after that band had stopped. Grohl recorded the self-titled debut album of 1995 almost entirely on his own in six days. When labels showed interest, he brought in the bassist Nate Mendel and the drummer William Goldsmith, both of Sunny Day Real Estate, and the guitarist Pat Smear, who had toured with Nirvana. The first gig was in February 1995, five months before the album appeared.

During the second album, The Colour and the Shape from 1997, Goldsmith left, after which Grohl re-recorded almost all of the drum parts. Taylor Hawkins became the new drummer. After that came There Is Nothing Left to Lose in 1999, One by One in 2002, the double album In Your Honor in 2005, partly acoustic and partly heavier, and Echoes, Silence, Patience & Grace in 2007. Wasting Light in 2011 was produced by Butch Vig, who had also made Nirvana's Nevermind. Sonic Highways in 2014 was the soundtrack to a television series by Grohl. After Hawkins's death in March 2022 came But Here We Are in 2023 and Your Favorite Toy in 2026.

The band plays melodic, powerful guitar rock with Grohl's screaming vocals and plenty of drive. The Foo Fighters have won fifteen Grammys, including five for best rock album, and are thus one of the most decorated rock groups. They showed that a band that emerged from the grunge era could fill stadiums for decades.
artiest/foo-fighters.listen: Listen to a track from The Colour and the Shape and notice how Grohl's drums and the sharp guitars come together with the vocal melody in a catchy chorus.

artiest/foreigner.text:
Foreigner is a British-American rock band that was formed in New York in 1976 by the English guitarist Mick Jones. He searched for a long time for the right musicians and found them in Ian McDonald, formerly of King Crimson, the drummer Dennis Elliott and the keyboard player Al Greenwood, among others. After dozens of auditions the singer Lou Gramm from Rochester joined. Because half of the members were British and the other half American, they were partly foreigners in each country. That is how the band got its name.

The debut album Foreigner was released in 1977, with Feels Like the First Time and Cold as Ice. After that came Double Vision (1978), with Hot Blooded, and Head Games (1979). The album 4 (1981) spent ten weeks at number one in the United States and contained Urgent, Juke Box Hero and the ballad Waiting for a Girl Like You. Agent Provocateur (1984) had the band's biggest hit, I Want to Know What Love Is, recorded with the New Jersey Mass Choir. Foreigner combined solid guitar riffs with keyboards, catchy choruses and Gramm's powerful voice.

Foreigner belongs to the bands that dominated American radio in the late 1970s and the 1980s with rock that was as much pop as rock. With I Want to Know What Love Is the group showed how a rock ballad with gospel influences can grow into a hit all over the world. In 2024 the band was inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame.
artiest/foreigner.listen: Listen to I Want to Know What Love Is and follow how the song grows: from a quiet beginning with keyboards and vocals to an ending in which a gospel choir sings along. Notice how Lou Gramm and the choir then alternate.

artiest/francesco-cavalli.text:
Francesco Cavalli, born Pietro Francesco Caletti-Bruni in 1602 in Crema, was a Venetian composer, organist and singer of the early Baroque. In 1616 he became a choirboy at San Marco in Venice, where Claudio Monteverdi became his teacher. He became second organist in 1639, first organist in 1665 and maestro di cappella in 1668. He took the name Cavalli from his patron, the nobleman Federico Cavalli. He wrote a great deal of church music, but is remembered mainly for his operas. His first opera, Le nozze di Teti e di Peleo, dates from 1639, shortly after the first public opera house in Venice, the Teatro San Cassiano, had opened. From 1660 to 1662 he worked in Paris, where he revived Xerse and premiered Ercole amante.

Cavalli succeeded Monteverdi as the most important opera composer of the mid-seventeenth century. He wrote more than thirty operas, almost all premiered in Venice. His best-known are Ormindo from 1644, Giasone from 1649 and La Calisto from 1651. Instead of the large court orchestra of Monteverdi's Mantua, he used a small orchestra of strings and basso continuo, suited to the public opera houses.

He brought melodic arias and folk-like figures into his librettos, with a strong sense of dramatic effect and a grotesque kind of humour. His operas show how, in half a century, opera grew from a new art form into a popular public spectacle. He died in Venice in 1676.
artiest/francesco-cavalli.listen: Listen to an aria from La Calisto and notice how the singing voice stays close to spoken language, accompanied by a small ensemble of strings and continuo.

artiest/francis-lai.text: Francis Lai (1932–2018) was born in Nice, the son of market gardeners of Italian descent. In Marseille he discovered jazz. In Paris he became part of the musical world of Montmartre. He wrote songs and accompanied Édith Piaf. In 1965 he met the director Claude Lelouch. Their first film together was Un homme et une femme (1966). The music was recorded in advance, and Lelouch played it on set to inspire the actors. Lai often worked with Lelouch afterwards, including on Vivre pour vivre (1967). For Love Story (1970) he won an Oscar. That soundtrack reached number two on the American Billboard chart. Lai wrote music for more than a hundred films and some six hundred songs.
artiest/francis-lai.listen: Notice how a single simple, singing melody carries the whole piece and keeps returning, with a small line-up and a calm rhythm.

artiest/francis-poulenc.text:
Francis Poulenc was a French composer and pianist, born in Paris in 1899 as the only son of a well-to-do manufacturer. His father expected him to join the family business, and he was not allowed to attend a conservatoire. He studied with the pianist Ricardo Viñes, who became his mentor, and got to know Erik Satie. Under Satie's influence he belonged to the young composers known as Les Six. His early work stood out for its playfulness and irreverence, such as the piano suite Mouvements perpétuels from 1919 and the ballet Les Biches from 1923.

In the 1930s a more serious side emerged, above all in the religious music he wrote from 1936 and alternated with lighter works. Among his best-known compositions are the Concert champêtre for harpsichord and orchestra from 1928, the organ concerto from 1938, the opera Dialogues des Carmélites from 1957 and the Gloria from 1959. As a pianist he performed with the baritone Pierre Bernac and the soprano Denise Duval, with whom he travelled through Europe and America. He recognised the importance of the gramophone early on and recorded a great deal from 1928.

For a long time he was known mainly as a humorous, light composer, and his religious music was overlooked. In the twenty-first century his serious works are receiving more attention, with new productions of Dialogues des Carmélites and La Voix humaine. His songs and choral works are often performed. He died in 1963.
artiest/francis-poulenc.listen: Listen to the Gloria and notice how cheerful, almost dancing passages alternate with quiet, devout moments, and how soprano, choir and orchestra follow one another in them.

artiest/francisco-alves.text:
Francisco de Morais Alves was a Brazilian singer, better known as Francisco Alves, Chico Alves or Chico Viola. He was born on 19 August 1898 and was regarded in the first half of the twentieth century as one of Brazil's most popular singers. Many consider him the greatest of his country. The quality of his work confirmed that status as early as 1933.

He recorded more than five hundred 78 rpm records, including the first electrical recording made in Brazil. He sang songs by composers such as Cartola, Heitor dos Prazeres and Ismael Silva. One of his best-known recordings is Aquarela do Brasil from 1939, the song by Ary Barroso, which he was the first to record. Alves was killed in 1952 in a car accident on the Rodovia Presidente Dutra, near Pindamonhangaba.

His time was the time of radio and the 78 rpm record. Alves belonged to the singers who spread samba to a large audience throughout Brazil. Aquarela do Brasil later became one of the best-known Brazilian songs outside the country. His voice, powerful and direct, suits the samba-canção of those years, in which the orchestra supports the singer and the lyrics carry the song.
artiest/francisco-alves.listen: Listen to Aquarela do Brasil and notice how the singer delivers the lyrics clearly and exuberantly above an orchestra with plenty of percussion. Can you hear the samba rhythms underneath?

artiest/franco.text:
Franco was the stage name of François Luambo Luanzo Makiadi, a Congolese guitarist, singer and bandleader. He was born in 1938 in Sona-Bata and grew up in Kinshasa. As a teenager he was taught by older musicians and played for the label Loningisa. There, in 1954, the producer Henri Bowane gave him the name Franco. In 1956 he founded OK Jazz together with others, the band he would later lead for many years.

In 1971 the band was renamed TPOK Jazz, the Tout-Puissant Orchestre Kinois de Jazz. In its day it was the most popular and influential band in Africa. Franco played Congolese rumba, with a flowing rhythm and a style of guitar playing all his own. He plucked the strings with thumb and index finger and gave the sebene, the lively guitar section, a place at the end of the song. That approach formed the basis of the so-called OK Jazz School. His early recordings from the 1950s, such as Joséphine Naboyi Ye, made Congolese rumba known across a large part of Africa.

Franco sang about love, marriage, rivalry and politics. In the 1970s he came close to the regime of President Mobutu and wrote songs in honour of its policies. In the 1980s the band remained productive, even when many members moved to Europe, with tracks such as Mamou and Mario. He died in Belgium in 1989. Note: in a text about album covers, the course mentions the Spain of the dictator Franco, a different man. This page is about the Congolese musician.
artiest/franco.listen: Listen to Mario by Franco et son TPOK Jazz. Notice how the guitar playing in the sebene keeps repeating the same pattern and how the vocals play over it.

artiest/franco-en-le-tpok-jazz.text:
TPOK Jazz was the orchestra of the Congolese guitarist, singer and composer Franco Luambo, born François Luambo Luanzo Makiadi. He was born on 6 July 1938 in Sona-Bata, in what was then the Belgian Congo, and grew up in Kinshasa. As a boy he became fascinated by the emerging Congolese rumba. He learned from musicians such as Paul Ebengo Dewayon and Albert Luampasi. In 1956 he founded OK Jazz together with others. In 1970 he took over full leadership, and in 1971 the band was given the name Tout-Puissant Orchestre Kinois de Jazz, the all-powerful jazz orchestra of Kinshasa.

Franco was lead guitarist and developed a recognisable style with intricate, rhythmic guitar lines. In doing so he laid the foundation for the so-called OK Jazz school. For more than twenty years the orchestra was the most popular and influential group in Africa. In 1976 Franco was appointed Officer of the National Order of the Leopard, and in 1982 he received the Maracas d'Or. He died on 12 October 1989. Mario from 1985 is one of the late tracks in his repertoire.

The music of TPOK Jazz is Congolese rumba with many guitars, a horn section and multi-part vocals, with long pieces in which the rhythm intensifies. Franco became a central figure in the African popular music of the twentieth century. His orchestra showed how African music developed freely, independent of the Western charts.
artiest/franco-en-le-tpok-jazz.listen: Listen to Mario and follow the guitars: notice how several guitar lines complement one another and how the music steps up a gear after the first section. What do the singers do in between?

artiest/francois-couperin.text:
François Couperin was a French Baroque composer, organist and harpsichordist. He was born on 10 November 1668 in Paris and died on 11 September 1733. To distinguish him from other musicians in his family he was called Couperin le Grand, Couperin the Great. His father Charles was organist at the Parisian church of Saint-Gervais, a post previously held by his uncle Louis Couperin, a famous keyboard player. As a boy François lost his father, and an organist from court circles took over his training. In 1690 his first publication appeared, Pièces d'orgue, a collection of organ masses.

In 1713 he applied for a royal privilege to publish his music, and used it at once for the first of four books of keyboard music, Pièces de clavecin. Les barricades mystérieuses comes from the second book, which was published in 1717. His last publications were Pièces de violes in 1728 and the fourth book of keyboard music. In the 1720s his health gradually failed him, and in 1730 his daughter Marguerite-Antoinette took his place as harpsichordist at court.

His keyboard music consists of short pieces with picturesque titles, full of ornaments and a fine feeling for sound. The harpsichord cannot make its notes swell, so Couperin wrote melodies full of trills and embellishments that make the line sing. He is one of the most important composers of the French Baroque. His work shows how music without drums and without harsh sounds can still have a pulse and character of its own.
artiest/francois-couperin.listen: Listen to Les barricades mystérieuses on the harpsichord and notice the continuous, undulating line in the right hand. Can you hear how the notes keep half blending into one another, without the sound growing louder or softer?

artiest/francois-xavier-roth.text:
François-Xavier Roth is a French conductor, born on 6 November 1971. He is the son of the organist Daniel Roth and began as a flautist himself. At the Conservatoire National Supérieur de Musique in Paris he studied flute with Alain Marion and conducting with János Fürst. In 2000 he won the Donatella Flick Conducting Competition, after which he was assistant to the London Symphony Orchestra for two years. He also worked as an assistant to John Eliot Gardiner.

In 2003 Roth founded the orchestra Les Siècles. This ensemble plays each piece on instruments from the period in which it was written, from the late Baroque and the Classical period to the twentieth century. In this way Ravel sounds on instruments of Ravel's own kind. For the hundredth anniversary of Le Sacre du printemps in 2013 the orchestra performed the work on period instruments at the BBC Proms and at the Alte Oper in Frankfurt. The recording of Le Sacre du printemps and Petrouchka was released in 2014. Also released were Symphonie fantastique, La mer and Daphnis et Chloé, among others, and a series of the tone poems of Richard Strauss. For French television he made the series Presto! with Les Siècles.

Roth led the orchestras of Baden-Baden and Freiburg, among others, and from 2015 to 2025 was Generalmusikdirektor of Cologne. Since 2017 he has been principal guest conductor of the London Symphony Orchestra. His significance lies in historically informed performance of nineteenth- and twentieth-century music, a field in which that approach was long less common than in Baroque music.
artiest/francois-xavier-roth.listen: Listen to an excerpt from Le Sacre du printemps by Les Siècles and notice the sound of the woodwinds and the brass. On instruments from 1913 they sound rougher and more colourful than in a modern performance.

artiest/francy-boland.text:
Francy Boland, in full François Boland, was a Belgian jazz pianist, composer and arranger. He was born on 6 November 1929 in Namur and died on 12 August 2005 in Geneva. He received a classical training and first attracted attention in 1949. In Belgium he played with Bobby Jaspar and Sadi, among others, including in the Bob Shots. In 1955 he joined Chet Baker's quintet.

After that Boland moved to the United States, where he arranged for Count Basie, Benny Goodman, Woody Herman and Dizzy Gillespie. With the drummer Kenny Clarke he led an octet, whose recordings were released on Blue Note, such as The Golden Eight from 1961. Back in Europe he became Kurt Edelhagen's most important arranger. In 1961, with a rhythm section built around Clarke, the bassist Jimmy Woode and himself, he founded the Kenny Clarke Francy Boland Big Band.

That big band quickly became one of the most famous to exist outside the United States, with albums such as Out of the Background and Open Space in 1967 and 1969. After it broke up in 1972, Boland concentrated on composing. From 1976 he lived mainly in Switzerland and wrote arrangements for Sarah Vaughan, among others. His importance lies in the proof that large-orchestra jazz could also take on a distinctive, high-quality form in Europe.
artiest/francy-boland.listen: Listen to a track by the Clarke Boland Big Band and notice how the arranger lets the saxophones and the brass answer as separate groups. Try to hear where the band stops and a soloist is left alone.

artiest/frank-boeijen.text:
Frank Boeijen was born on 27 November 1957 in Nijmegen, the youngest in a Catholic family of ten children. Through his older brothers he got to know the music of Bob Dylan and Neil Young. In 1977 he released an album independently with the guitarist Wout Pennings, which was later re-recorded under the direction of Rob de Nijs.

In 1979 he founded the Frank Boeijen Groep, which performed for the first time on 3 November of that year at the Nijmegen youth centre Doornroosje. The debut album appeared in 1981, with the single Transport uit Bangkok. The breakthrough came in 1983 with the album 1001 Hotel and the Motown-influenced hit Linda. After that came Zwart wit (1984) and Kronenburg Park (1985), about a prostitute in the Nijmegen park, with backing vocals by Mai Tai. In the second half of the 1980s the group, with fewer synthesizers and a little saxophone, made a trilogy of albums and played in theatres instead of clubs, which was unusual at the time. In 1991 Boeijen disbanded the group.

The Frank Boeijen Groep belonged to the wave of Dutch-language pop music in the 1980s and made new wave in their own language. Boeijen wrote poetic, often melancholy lyrics to melodic music somewhere between pop and chanson. As a solo artist he continued to tour in the Netherlands and Belgium afterwards and made many more albums. In 2005 he received an Edison for his contribution to Dutch music.
artiest/frank-boeijen.listen: Listen to Kronenburg Park (1985). Notice how Boeijen tells the story of a woman in the park in a restrained way, and the backing vocals of the girl group Mai Tai in the chorus.
